thread:
elaine: Quick intake — opal-8b repo: https://git.example/opal-8b. License header says 'Custom Research License v1' but another doc in the repo references 'non-commercial' use. We want to evaluate for Dedicated + Private and run quant experiments. Can we host quantized weights and redistribute compiled artifacts to customers? Any red flags on export control or data provenance?

josh: cc @legal @sana — want a short checklist we can follow before any bring-up.

legal-bot: Need the full license text attached to the intake ticket. 'Non-commercial' usually blocks paid/hosted access. Also check upstream training data provenance (PII, scraped sources).

sana: Ran a quick int8 quant pass locally — perf looks reasonable. But redistribution of derived weights is the primary legal question. If license forbids derivatives, we cannot ship quantized binaries.

maria: If it's strictly NC, we could maybe use it for internal evals on Private infra but not enable for paying customers. We need clarity before any Dedicated offering.

grant: Can we ask upstream for a commercial addendum? Who's our contact? If they can sign a hosting/redistribution addendum, great.

elaine: I'll open the intake ticket (RL-INTAKE-432) and attach repo + license. @legal can you draft a short email template to request: commercial license, permission to host quantized/optimized binaries, and an ECCN/export classification?

legal-bot: Draft template ready — asks for: 1) full license grant text, 2) explicit permission for redistribution of derived weights and optimized artifacts, 3) export control classification (ECCN), 4) confirmation of training-data provenance. Placing template here: https://docs.internal/opal-licence-template. Use it in the intake ticket.

sana: Suggest adding an engineering checklist entry: - license attached to intake - quantization allowed? - allowed hosting modes (hosted/dedicated/private) - redistribution rules - model artifact checksums and provenance - export control flag. I'll put it in the bring-up playbook.

maria: :thumbsup: Also add a step to block public default rollout until legal signoff. Internal-only canary is fine after written clearance.

ops-bot: infra task created: infra/opal8b-canary-private. ETA 48h after license clearance.

elaine: Action items summarized: 1) @legal send template/request (due EOD) 2) @elaine open RL-INTAKE-432 + attach license 3) @sana run full quant reg tests and record artifacts (due 2026-03-27) 4) infra run private canary after green.

josh: Small note: compliance wants ECCN looped in early for potential export controls on optimized weights. cc @compliance.

compliance: Acknowledge — we'll review ECCN once upstream responds. If labeled 'research-only' that's a blocker for customer hosting.

maria: Holding public rollouts until legal + compliance clear. Keep updates in the intake ticket.

legal-bot: Quick guidance: if upstream provides a 'research only' license → cannot commercially host or redistribute. If they can sign a hosting/redistribution addendum, mark intake as "clear for bring-up" and then follow the usual canary + eval gating.

elaine: Thanks everyone — I'll update RL-INTAKE-432 with this thread and chase upstream contact now.
